en: Are you free this Saturday evening?
context: Asking a friend if they can meet.
explain: We use 'Are you free' to ask if someone has time. It is a polite, easy way to start making plans.

alt.en: Do you have time this Saturday?

en: Let's meet at the bus stand at five.
context: Fixing a time and place with a friend.
explain: 'Let's' + base verb is used to suggest a plan together. Add the place and time after it.

en: I haven't seen you for ages!
context: Meeting an old friend after a long time.
explain: 'Haven't seen' with 'for ages' means a very long time without meeting. It sounds warm and friendly.

alt.en: It's been so long since we met!

en: Can you help me move this table?
tamil: இந்த மேசையை நகர்த்த எனக்கு உதவ முடியுமா?
context: Asking a neighbour or friend for physical help.
explain: 'Can you' + verb is a simple way to ask for help. Say please to be extra polite.

en: Thanks for helping me with my project.
context: Thanking a friend after they helped.
explain: After 'thanks for' we use the -ing form of the verb. It shows you are grateful.

en: I'm really sorry I forgot your birthday.
tamil: உன் பிறந்தநாளை மறந்ததுக்கு நான் உண்மையிலேயே வருந்துறேன்.
context: Apologising to a friend for a mistake.
explain: 'Really sorry' makes the apology stronger. Then say what you did in the past tense.

en: I didn't mean to hurt you.
context: Apologising after saying something unkind.
explain: 'Didn't mean to' + verb says it was not on purpose. It is a gentle way to say sorry.

en: Please forgive me, it was my mistake.
context: A sincere apology when you are at fault.
explain: 'Please forgive me' is a polite request for pardon. Admitting 'my mistake' shows honesty.

en: We're having a small get-together at home tomorrow.
tamil: நாளைக்கு வீட்டுல ஒரு சின்ன கெட்-டுகெதர் இருக்கு.
context: Inviting friends to a small party.
explain: We use the present continuous for a fixed plan in the near future. 'Tomorrow' makes the time clear.

en: Would you like to join us for lunch?
context: Inviting a colleague or friend to eat with you.
explain: 'Would you like to' is a polite way to invite someone. Use it with people you do not know well.

alt.en: Come and have lunch with us.

en: I'll definitely come to your wedding.
context: Accepting an invitation with enthusiasm.
explain: 'I'll' shows a promise or decision. 'Definitely' tells the person you are sure.

en: Sorry, I can't make it tonight.
tamil: மன்னிச்சிடு, இன்னிக்கு ராத்திரி என்னால வர முடியாது.
context: Politely refusing an invitation.
explain: 'Can't make it' is a common spoken way to say you cannot attend. Say sorry first to stay polite.

en: What should I do about my noisy neighbour?
tamil: என் சத்தம் போடுற பக்கத்து வீட்டுக்காரரை என்ன பண்றது?
context: Asking a friend for advice about a problem.
explain: 'What should I do' asks for advice. It is a very natural question between friends.

en: You should talk to him calmly.
context: Giving advice to a friend.
explain: 'Should' + verb gives friendly advice. 'Calmly' tells how to do it.

en: Don't stress, everything will be fine.
context: Comforting a friend who is stressed.
explain: 'Don't worry' is an imperative that comforts. 'Will be' shows hope for the future.

alt.en: Relax, it will all work out.

en: If I were you, I would ask her directly.
tamil: நான் உன் இடத்துல இருந்தா, அவகிட்ட நேரடியா கேப்பேன்.
context: Giving advice in a gentle way.
explain: 'If I were you' is a polite pattern for advice. It uses 'would' + base verb.

en: My colleague Ravi has become a close friend.
tamil: என் கூட வேலை செய்யுற ரவி இப்போ நெருக்கமான நண்பனாயிட்டான்.
context: Talking about a coworker who became a friend.
explain: 'Has become' links the past change to now. 'Colleague' means a person you work with.

en: We used to sit together in the canteen.
context: Remembering old office days with a friend.
explain: 'Used to' + verb talks about a past habit that has stopped. It is common in friendly chats.

en: Do you want to grab a tea after work?
context: Inviting a colleague for tea.
explain: 'Grab a tea' is casual spoken English for 'have a quick tea'. It sounds friendly and relaxed.

alt.en: Shall we have tea after office?

en: My neighbour always waters our plants when we travel.
tamil: நாங்க வெளியூர் போகும்போது எங்க பக்கத்து வீட்டுக்காரர் எப்பவும் செடிகளுக்குத் தண்ணி ஊத்துவார்.
context: Describing a helpful neighbour.
explain: We use the simple present with 'always' for a regular habit. 'When we travel' tells the time.

en: Could you keep an eye on my house while I'm away?
tamil: நான் ஊர்ல இல்லாதப்ப என் வீட்டைக் கொஞ்சம் கவனிச்சுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a neighbour for a small favour.
explain: 'Keep an eye on' means watch something carefully. 'Could you' is a polite request.

en: He is shy, but he is very kind.
tamil: அவன் கூச்ச சுபாவம், ஆனா ரொம்ப நல்லவன்.
context: Describing a friend's nature.
explain: 'But' joins two ideas that are different. It is a simple way to describe a person fairly.

en: I met my best friend at college.
tamil: என் உயிர் நண்பனை நான் காலேஜ்ல சந்திச்சேன்.
context: Telling how you met a close friend.
explain: 'Met' is the past form of 'meet'. Use 'at' before places like college or school.

en: We have been friends since school.
context: Talking about a long friendship.
explain: 'Have been' + 'since' shows something that started in the past and continues now.

alt.en: We have known each other for years.

en: Thank you for always standing by me.
context: Telling a friend you appreciate them.
explain: 'Standing by me' means supporting me in hard times. It is a warm, heartfelt thank you.

en: Why didn't you call me yesterday?
context: Asking a friend why they did not call.
explain: 'Why didn't you' asks for a reason in the past. A friendly tone keeps it from sounding angry.

en: I'm going to visit my friend in Madurai next week.
tamil: அடுத்த வாரம் மதுரையில இருக்கற என் நண்பனைப் பார்க்கப் போறேன்.
context: Sharing a plan to meet a friend.
explain: 'Going to' + verb talks about a plan you already made. Add the place and time at the end.

en: Please don't tell anyone my secret.
context: Asking a friend to keep a secret.
explain: 'Please don't' + verb is a polite way to ask someone not to do something.

en: She never complains, even when she is tired.
tamil: அவ களைப்பா இருந்தாலும் ஒரு நாளும் குறை சொல்ல மாட்டா.
context: Praising a patient friend.
explain: 'Never' makes the sentence negative. 'Even when' adds a surprise: she is tired but still does not complain.

en: Let's sort this out like friends.
context: Suggesting to solve an argument calmly.
explain: 'Sort out' means solve a problem. 'Like friends' reminds both people to stay kind.

en: I'm so glad you came today.
tamil: நீ இன்னிக்கு வந்ததுல எனக்கு ரொம்ப சந்தோஷம்.
context: Welcoming a guest at home.
explain: 'Glad' is a happy feeling. Use 'so' to make it stronger and friendlier.

en: Come in and make yourself at home.
tamil: உள்ளே வாங்க, சொந்த வீடு மாதிரி இருங்க.
context: Welcoming a friend or neighbour into your house.
explain: 'Make yourself at home' tells a guest to relax and feel comfortable. It is a warm welcome.

alt.en: Please come in and sit down.

en: My neighbours invited us for dinner on Diwali.
tamil: தீபாவளி அன்னிக்கு எங்க பக்கத்து வீட்டுக்காரங்க எங்களை சாப்பாட்டுக்குக் கூப்பிட்டாங்க.
context: Talking about a neighbour's invitation.
explain: 'Invited us for dinner' is the correct pattern: invite + person + for + meal.

en: Will you be able to come to my house-warming?
context: Inviting someone to a new-home function.
explain: 'Will you be able to' asks about someone's ability or chance to attend in the future.

en: I'm sorry, I'm running late.
context: Telling a friend you are delayed.
explain: 'Running late' means you will arrive after the planned time. Say sorry and update them quickly.

en: He lent me money when I really needed it.
tamil: எனக்கு உண்மையிலேயே தேவைப்பட்டப்ப அவன் பணம் கொடுத்து உதவினான்.
context: Talking about a friend who helped you.
explain: 'Lent' is the past form of 'lend'. Use 'when' to give the time of the help.

en: Any plans for this weekend?
tamil: இந்த வார இறுதிக்கு ஏதாவது ப்ளான் இருக்கா?
context: Starting a chat to plan something together.
explain: 'Any plans for' is a short spoken question. It is a common way to open an invitation.

en: You are always welcome at our place.
context: Telling a friend they can visit any time.
explain: 'Welcome' here means you are happy to have them. 'Our place' is casual for 'our home'.

en: Can I ask you for a small favour?
context: Politely starting a request.
explain: 'Ask for a favour' is the usual phrase. 'Small' makes the request sound light and easy.

en: They have lived next door to us for ten years.
tamil: அவங்க எங்க பக்கத்து வீட்டுல பத்து வருஷமா இருக்காங்க.
context: Describing a long-time neighbour.
explain: 'Have lived' + 'for ten years' shows a situation that started in the past and is still true.

en: A good friend listens without judging.
context: Sharing an idea about real friendship.
explain: The simple present is used for general truths. 'Without judging' uses -ing after a preposition.

en: We'll stay in touch, I promise.
context: Saying goodbye to a friend who is moving away.
explain: 'Stay in touch' means keep contact by calls or messages. 'I promise' adds feeling.
